cards.front: Recall a key point about Promotion
cards.back: Advertising: paid communication through media channels (TV, radio, print, online, social media, billboards). It builds awareness and brand image but is expensive and difficult to measure ROI directly.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Promotion
cards.back: Sales promotion: short-term incentives to encourage purchase (BOGOF, discounts, coupons, free gifts, competitions). Boosts immediate sales but can damage brand image if overused.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Promotion
cards.back: Public relations (PR): managing the business's image through media coverage, press releases, events, and community involvement. It's credible (not paid for) but the business can't control the message.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Promotion
cards.back: Personal selling: one-to-one communication (sales reps, demonstrations). Effective for high-value, complex products but expensive per customer and limited reach.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Promotion
cards.back: Digital promotion: social media marketing, influencer partnerships, email campaigns, SEO, and content marketing. Cost-effective, highly targeted, measurable, but requires ongoing content creation and platform expertise.

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating promotional methods, use the TAM framework: Target market reach (does it reach the right people?), Affordability (does it fit the budget?), Measurability (can the business track results?). The best promotional mix combines methods that work at different stages of the AIDA model.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Social media marketing is free, so it's the best option for all businesses. Correct: While creating social media accounts is free, effective social media marketing requires: paid advertising spend (organic reach is very limited), content creation (photos, videos, copywriting), staff time for management and engagement, and potentially influencer fees. AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Promotion with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

Promotion is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying Promotion to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For promotion, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with promotion. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of promotion on a business.

GCSE Business exam questions about promotion range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions. For definition questions (1-2 marks), give a precise business definition. For explanation questions (3-4 marks), define and explain with a brief example. For analysis questions (6-9 marks), develop a chain of reasoning showing cause and effect.
